verdict.reason: The code is present as quoted (mark-ready.mjs:175 vs harness.config.json:52-62), but it is not a blocking design-fit defect. (a) The two lists answer different questions: `ciConfig` decides how much CI runs plus the label/CODEOWNERS mirror (harness.config.json:3,51; .github/CODEOWNERS:42-61), while CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES decides whether the executed workflow definition itself came from the branch. They are not interchangeable — reusing `ciConfig` would refuse auto-promotion for every package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml change, a far broader behavior than gate 1b's job — so this is not "duplicated logic giving two answers to the same question". (b) The implementation matches the canonical subsystem doc verbatim (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1905-1921 specifies exactly `.github/workflows/**` and `.github/actions/**`, renames on both names, fail-closed), so design-doc discipline is met and this is not a parallel invention. (c) The alleged overclaim is not one: mark-ready.mjs:320-322 is scoped to "the CI file", which the gate does establish, and the report line mark-ready.mjs:238 names its own scope explicitly. (d) The residual hole (branch-supplied scripts/verify-*.mjs) is an explicitly recorded deferral — harness-engineering.md:524-540 states the property guards mistakes, not a hostile author, and Phase 5 of docs/tasks/active/20260812-path-aware-ci-todo.md:255-260 tracks the mechanical fix; merge still needs a human approval and code-owner review of scripts/verify-*.mjs (.github/CODEOWNERS:60-61), and mark-ready only flips draft->ready (mark-ready.mjs:41-44). Under this lens that is at most `minor` ("reuse that was available but not required", cost internal to the codebase), and minor never blocks; the broader tamper-coverage argument belongs to the security lens.
